p: The Ocean Explorer Centre is part of the Scottish Association for Marine Science site at Dunstaffnage, just outside Oban, and that location brings a bonus. Dunstaffnage Castle, a mighty medieval fortress on a rocky outcrop, is a short hop away. It's cared for by Historic Environment Scotland and has a lovely ruined chapel in the woods nearby.

For a beach, head to Ganavan Sands, a sandy bay on the northern edge of Oban with views across to the islands. It's great for a paddle, a picnic and a spot of rock-pooling, so kids can go looking for the creatures they've just learned about.

Out on the water, the summer months bring the chance to spot seals, dolphins and seabirds, and with luck even minke whales or basking sharks further out around the islands. Wildlife boat trips leave from Oban, and the CalMac ferries to Mull and beyond give you a cheap and cheerful way to scan the sea for fins.
The tiny island of Kerrera, just across the bay, is reached by a short passenger ferry and makes a peaceful walk with views back to town.
